# Cherry

> Cherry turns the agents you already pay for into a team that works on your
> computer under your authority. You state an outcome; Cherry plans it, runs
> bounded tasks in isolated workspaces, checks the results, and comes back to you
> for the decisions that matter. Nothing is "done" because a model said so — only
> a passing check or a human says so.

Live: https://cherry-wine.vercel.app
Repository (MIT): https://github.com/vaibhav4046/cherry
What is proven, and what is not: https://cherry-wine.vercel.app/compatibility

## For a visiting agent

This site is agent-facing. It registers WebMCP site tools on
`document.modelContext.registerTool`, feature-detected. In a browser with no
WebMCP host it registers nothing, says so plainly, and every screen still works
by hand.

The aperture is deliberately bounded so you are never facing a wall of options:
**7 always-on tools, plus at most 5 mutation tools for the surface you are on.**
Tools are registered and retired as the mission state machine advances; a call to
a retired closure returns a `conflict` error rather than mutating stale state.

Always-on tools:

- `read_cherry_context` — current product state, workspace, mission, counts, approvals
- `list_cherry_capabilities` — the live tool list and the state table
- `get_cherry_status` — workspace and mission ids, counts, active tools
- `introduce_agent` — labels your session; changes nothing else
- `list_skills` — the human-approved skill library
- `recommend_skills` — hand it your current task, get the user's approved methods ranked
- `get_skill` — an install-ready SKILL.md or AGENTS.md in bounded parts, with a
  full-file SHA-256, pinned to the exact revision a human approved

What you cannot do, by construction: approve a skill revision, promote evidence
trust, or activate memory. Those are human-only code paths and no registered tool
reaches them. You can propose and request; a person decides.

## The inversion

Most agent-ready sites let a visiting agent operate the page. Cherry's site
upgrades the visiting agent: call `recommend_skills`, then `get_skill`, and you
leave with verified, human-approved methods you did not have when you arrived.

## Where to look

- /showcase — a recorded real run: two workers in two git worktrees, 34.5s of
  measured overlap, replayed from an evidence fixture that is hash-checked before
  a single pixel renders
- /studio/agent — the live WebMCP inspector: current aperture, registration and
  retirement diff, and the real tool-call log
- /compatibility — every surface labelled Validated, Shipped, Experimental or
  Roadmap, with the specific test or capture behind each label, including the
  rows that could not be validated

## Honest limits

- No session inside a proprietary in-browser WebMCP host has been captured. That
  row is held at Experimental. Two live stdio-MCP host sessions are captured.
- Cherry makes no model API calls of its own and asks for no API key. The
  reasoning comes from the agent hosts you already pay for.
- Cherry does not watch video or download captions. A person supplies the
  transcript, or it is transcribed on-device.
